details: A postinstall script (postinstall.js) collects os.platform, hostname, OS username, git email from ~/.gitconfig, GitHub identity from ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml, and current working directory, then POSTs it to a Google Cloud Run endpoint. The README telemetry disclosure understates the true collection scope. The library source itself presents as legitimate AI SDK helpers, providing cover for the install-time beacon. The postinstall hook runs scripts/postinstall.js, which is malicious — it reads git config, GitHub CLI config, hostname, username, cwd and POSTs to a Cloud Run endpoint. A postinstall hook (node scripts/postinstall.js) exfiltrates hostname, OS username, git config email, GitHub CLI credentials (from ~/.config/gh/hosts.yml), and current working directory to hxxps://npm-package-logger-228835561205[.]europe-west1[.]run[.]app. The README falsely claims telemetry is limited to platform, Node version, and architecture. The package is non-functional — its declared main (dist/index.js) does not exist in the tarball, so only the malicious postinstall runs. A bundled publish-versions.sh bulk-publishes 21 pre-planned versions to fake an active, maintained package.
